results.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
results.proof_sketch: If G-S has a cycle, choose a shortest one. It is chordless in the induced subgraph G-S and hence induced in G. Bipartiteness makes its length even. An induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices, so every possible shortest cycle has length 4, 6, or 8. This proves the hitting equivalence. When S is an FVS, each component of G-S is a tree. A tree of diameter at least 7 contains an induced eight-vertex path, so every component has diameter at most 6 and radius at most 3. If S is inclusion-minimal and x∈S, restoring x creates a cycle. Its remaining vertices lie in G-S, so its two neighbors of x belong to one tree component.

results.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
results.proof_sketch: Enumerate every 4-, 6-, and 8-vertex subset inducing a cycle. By the first claim, feedback vertex sets are exactly the transversals of this rank-eight hypergraph. Given an unhit hyperedge, every solution selects at least one of its at most eight vertices; branching over those choices gives O(8^k) nodes, with O(n^8) work per node. For approximation, greedily form a maximal vertex-disjoint collection of listed cycles and return their union U. Maximality makes U a transversal and therefore an FVS. If p cycles were selected, every FVS has size at least p, while |U|≤8p.

results.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
results.proof_sketch: An exact exhaustive enumeration introduces vertices in the order of a required Hamilton path. Bipartiteness permits only opposite-parity earlier neighbors and forces the predecessor edge. Extensions creating a C4 or an induced P8 are rejected; such earlier violations cannot be repaired later. The numbers of admissible ordered graphs at orders 1 through 15 are exactly 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0. Hence no graph in the subclass contains a simple path on 15 vertices. In an undirected DFS forest every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints, and every root-to-leaf path therefore has at most 14 vertices. Bags consisting of each DFS vertex and all its ancestors form a tree decomposition of width at most 13. A fixed-width connectivity-partition dynamic program computes an exact minimum FVS in polynomial time.

results.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
results.proof_sketch: Iterative deepening that branches over the four vertices of a detected C4 finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. The graph G-X is C4-free, P8-free, and bipartite, so the preceding claim constructs a width-13 decomposition. Adding X to every bag gives a decomposition of G of width at most r+13. On a nice decomposition, store the deleted bag subset and the connectivity partition of retained bag vertices. Edge and join transitions reject precisely combinations that create a cycle. The number of states is 2^{O(r log r)} per bag, yielding the stated exact FPT bound.

results.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
results.proof_sketch: For the half graph H_n with a_i b_j iff i≤j, neighborhoods are strictly nested, so there are no false twins; it is 2K2-free and hence P5-free. Keeping all B and a_{n-1},a_n shows that n-2 deletions suffice to destroy every C4. Conversely, for the two smallest retained A-indices i<j, C4-freeness permits at most one retained b_l with l≥j, bounding the retained graph by n+2 vertices; thus n-2 deletions are necessary. The graph formed by m internally disjoint length-three u-v paths is bipartite, C4-free, P8-free, 2-connected, and has order 2m+2. Finally, K_{3,3} is P4-free and has integral FVS optimum 2, whereas assigning 1/4 to each vertex satisfies every induced-C4 constraint with objective 3/2.

results.claim: Even false-twin-free P5-free bipartite graphs have simultaneously unbounded Feedback Vertex Set optimum and unbounded treewidth: for the half graph H_n, fvs(H_n)=n-2 and tw(H_n)≥⌈n/2⌉.
results.proof_sketch: Strictly nested neighborhoods within each bipartition class, and their membership in opposite sides, make all open neighborhoods distinct. Nestedness also forbids an induced 2K2; since every induced P5 contains an induced 2K2 on its first and last edges, H_n is P5-free. Deleting a_1,…,a_{n-2} leaves one four-vertex path and isolated vertices, so fvs(H_n)≤n-2. Conversely, a forest is C4-free. If at least two A-vertices survive, let a_i,a_j with i<j be the two smallest-index survivors. At most one surviving b_l has l≥j, while there are at most n-j+2 surviving A-vertices and at most j surviving B-vertices. Thus at most n+2 of the original 2n vertices survive, proving at least n-2 deletions; the case with at most one surviving A-vertex requires at least n-1. Finally, with t=⌈n/2⌉, the vertices a_1,…,a_t and b_t,…,b_n induce K_{t,n-t+1}, whose treewidth is t. Hence tw(H_n)≥t.

results.claim: The natural induced-short-cycle covering LP has integrality gap tending to 2 already on P4-free bipartite graphs: on K_{n,n}, its integral optimum is n-1, its fractional optimum is n/2, and the ratio is 2-2/n.
results.proof_sketch: Every induced cycle of K_{n,n} is a C4, and K_{n,n} is P4-free. Deleting n-1 vertices from one side leaves a star, whereas deleting at most n-2 total vertices leaves at least two vertices on each side and hence a C4. Thus the integral FVS and transversal optimum is n-1. Setting x_v=1/4 for every vertex satisfies every C4 constraint and has value n/2. There are binom(n,2)^2 C4 constraints, and each vertex occurs in (n-1)binom(n,2) of them. Summing all constraints therefore gives Σ_v x_v≥binom(n,2)^2/((n-1)binom(n,2))=n/2, proving fractional optimality. The gap is consequently (n-1)/(n/2)=2-2/n. The boundary n=2 has gap 1, n=3 recovers the audited K_{3,3} witness, and the ratio tends to 2.

results.claim: The factor 8 for the specific maximal-short-cycle-packing union algorithm is tight on P8-free bipartite graphs.
results.proof_sketch: Let G be the disjoint union of t≥1 chordless C8 components. It is bipartite and P8-free: an induced path is contained in one component, while the only eight-vertex induced subgraph of that component is C8 rather than P8. Every proper induced subgraph of a chordless cycle is a forest, so the only induced C4, C6, or C8 in each component is its full C8. Any maximal vertex-disjoint packing must therefore contain the C8 from every component, and the algorithm returns all 8t vertices. One deletion per component is necessary and sufficient for an FVS, so OPT=t and the returned ratio is exactly 8. This limits only that packing-union algorithm, not the possible approximation ratio of other methods.

results.claim: False-twin quotienting exactly preserves the P8-free bipartite setting: contracting every equal-open-neighborhood class to one representative produces a false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeleton H with class multiplicities q_v, and every false-twin blow-up of such an H is again P8-free and bipartite.
results.proof_sketch: Vertices with the same open neighborhood are nonadjacent, and adjacency between two distinct classes is complete, so choosing one representative per class defines the quotient skeleton H as an induced subgraph. Hence H inherits bipartiteness and P8-freeness. It is false-twin-free: equal neighborhoods of two quotient vertices would lift to equal unions of original classes, contradicting that they were distinct classes. Conversely, blow up each vertex v of a bipartite H into q_v independent vertices having the same neighbors. Bipartiteness is preserved. No induced P8 can contain two vertices of one class, because those vertices have equal neighborhoods within the eight-vertex induced subgraph, whereas all eight vertices of P8 have distinct open neighborhoods. Thus any induced P8 in the blow-up projects injectively, preserving every edge and nonedge, to an induced P8 in H. Therefore a P8-free skeleton has a P8-free blow-up.

results.claim:
Maximum induced forests admit an exact singleton-core/pendant-bundle normal form on the false-twin quotient. If H is the quotient and q_v is the size of class v, then
α_forest(G)=max_{U⊆V(H), H[U] a forest} (|U|+α_q(H[D_U])),
where D_U={v∉U:q_v>1 and |N_H(v)∩U|≤1} and α_q denotes maximum q-weight independent-set value.
results.proof_sketch: For a retained induced forest W, let r_v be the number retained from class v. If r_v≥2 and the class has two retained neighbor vertices, two class members and those two neighbors induce a C4; the neighbors are nonadjacent by bipartiteness. Hence such a class has at most one retained neighbor. If 1<r_v<q_v, all omitted twins can then be added as leaves or isolates, contradicting maximal cardinality. Thus some maximum forest has r_v∈{0,1,q_v}. Put in U the classes with r_v=1 and in L the classes with q_v>1 and r_v=q_v. Then H[U] is a forest, L is independent, and every vertex of L has at most one neighbor in U. Conversely, from any such U,L, retain one representative of every U-class and every vertex of every L-class. The U-part is a forest, while all retained vertices belonging to L are leaves or isolates, so the result is a forest. For fixed U, the feasible sets L are exactly the independent subsets of D_U, and their contribution is their q-weight. Maximizing first over L and then over U proves the formula. Minimum FVS size is |V(G)|−α_forest(G).

results.claim: The target is polynomial-time equivalent, with multiplicities measured in unary by Q=Σ_v q_v, to optimizing the quotient formula over false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeletons; for every fixed singleton core U, the optimal pendant-bundle completion is computable in polynomial time.
results.proof_sketch: Given G, equal-neighborhood classes, H, and q can be computed in polynomial time, Q=|V(G)|, and the preceding formula reconstructs an optimal retained forest by keeping one original vertex from each chosen U-class and all vertices from each chosen bundle class. Conversely, given H and unary multiplicities q, explicitly blowing up H has Q vertices and remains P8-free bipartite by the preceding claim; an FVS algorithm on that graph returns the quotient optimum through the same normal form. These are value- and solution-preserving reductions polynomial in Q. For fixed U, H[D_U] is bipartite, and α_q is polynomial-time computable: its complement is a minimum q-weight vertex cover, obtained by an s-t cut with source-to-left and right-to-sink capacities q_v and edge arcs of capacity greater than Σq_v. The unresolved optimization is therefore precisely the choice of the induced-forest core U. When every q_v=1, D_U is empty and this core problem is the original maximum-induced-forest problem on a false-twin-free instance, so the reformulation does not by itself solve the target.

final_writeup:
The independent audit reports no REFUTED or UNRESOLVED claims and verifies all eight parent claims. Those claims and proof sketches are preserved exactly. Its VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS target judgment remains controlling: the parameterized algorithms can be exponential when k or the C4-transversal number grows, the width bound applies only to the C4-free subclass, and the approximation is not an exact algorithm.

The required structural-reformulation lens yields an exact additional reduction. Partition the input into false-twin classes, take one representative from each class, and record its multiplicity. This produces a false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeleton, and false-twin blow-up preserves this graph class in both directions.

On this quotient, some maximum induced forest has a canonical form. Each class contributes either zero vertices, one singleton core vertex, or the entire class. An entire nonsingleton class can occur only as an isolated or pendant bundle attached to one singleton; two full adjacent classes would create a C4. Consequently, if U is the set of singleton classes, then H[U] must be a forest and the full bundle classes form an independent set among vertices having at most one neighbor in U. This gives the exact formula

α_forest(G)=max_{H[U] forest} (|U|+α_q(H[D_U])).

For fixed U, the second term is weighted independent set in a bipartite graph and is computable by one minimum-cut construction. Thus the full target is polynomial-time equivalent to selecting the singleton induced-forest core U in this quotient objective; all false-twin multiplicities can then be completed optimally in polynomial time. The equivalence is solution-preserving, and expansion is polynomial when multiplicities are measured by their total Q, as they are for a quotient of the original input.

This is a structural normal form, not a polynomial-time solution. In particular, false-twin-free inputs have q_v=1 everywhere, so the bundle term vanishes and choosing U is exactly the original maximum induced forest problem. The audited half graphs show that this irreducible core can still have unbounded optimum and treewidth. Therefore claimed_resolution remains PARTIAL. A complete solution must exploit additional structure of false-twin-free P8-free bipartite graphs, or optimize the displayed core objective without relying on bounded treewidth, bounded C4-transversal number, LP integrality, or the tight packing-union rule.
